notes.text: In Chinese the name echoes a thousand reds weeping together.
In Chinese the name echoes ten thousand beauties sharing grief.

Both [text missing] markers identify lacunae in the chosen Chinese source, not pauses in Bao-yu’s thoughts. The study’s name and the words after his supposition are missing; no wording from another edition has been supplied.

Bao-yu’s saying is translated in the sense he gives it next. Its wording can also be read as “Nearer kin should not separate remoter kin; the earlier should not overstep the later”, which pulls against his explanation.
The teasing turns on Xiang-yun’s saying ai (“love”) for er (“second”), hence “Dear Cousin” and the altered count. The further sound e joins the teasing at the end of the exchange.
